successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy model file exports a LeavePolicy interface and a CreateLeavePolicyDto, and imports LeaveType from the Phase 3 leave-type model (establishing the cross-entity dependency without redefining LeaveType).

The leave module barrel (index.ts) re-exports LeavePolicy, CreateLeavePolicyDto, ILeavePolicyRepository, and LeavePolicyRepository alongside the existing Phase 3 LeaveType exports, so downstream phases can import all leave types from the single public entry point.

The repository exposes all six operations — findByLeaveTypeId, findById, findAll, create, update, softDelete — and each persists/queries against the leave_policies table through the shared pg pool (no direct DB access outside the repository, satisfying GP-001).
create persists a new leave_policies row and returns the inserted LeavePolicy; when requiresManagerApproval or isActive are omitted from the DTO they default to true.
findById and findByLeaveTypeId return null / empty array respectively when no matching non-deleted row exists; findAll returns an empty array when the table has no non-deleted rows.

update with an empty partial DTO returns the existing non-deleted row without issuing an UPDATE; update on a non-existent id returns null; update on a deleted row returns null (deleted_at IS NULL guard).
softDelete sets deleted_at (and updated_at) and returns true when a row was affected, false when the id does not exist or is already soft-deleted; it does not physically remove the row.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.test.ts mock the shared pg pool and cover every repository method including happy-path, not-found/null, empty-array, optional-field-default, and no-fields-update cases; the suite passes under `npx jest`.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the LeavePolicyRepository is the only component that issues SQL against leave_policies.
Strict TypeScript with no implicit any and strict null checks; use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS no-any rule).

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the leave-policy model may import LeaveType from the sibling leave-type model within the same module, but external consumers must use the barrel.

No circular dependencies between modules; the leave-policy model/repository may depend on the leave-type model and shared db connection, but nothing in those dependencies may import back from leave-policy.
Unit tests must mock the shared pg pool (src/shared/db/connection) rather than hitting a real database; no integration/DB connectivity is required for this phase's tests.
outOfScope: LeaveBalance model and repository (Phase 5) — not created or referenced in this phase beyond the barrel not yet exporting it.
LeaveRequest model and repository (Phase 6) and the LeaveStatus-driven request lifecycle.
AuditLog model/repository and audit recording (Phase 7); this phase performs no audit writes even though create/update/softDelete are state-changing (audit is wired in the service phase).
Leave service, controller, and Fastify routes (Phases 8–9) — no HTTP surface, Zod validation, or RBAC enforcement belongs in this repository/model phase.
Database migrations / DDL for the leave_policies table; this phase assumes the table schema exists and only interacts via the pool.

ambiguities.description: The reconciled architecture (.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json) models accrualRate, maxAccumulation, and minimumNoticeDays as `number | null` (nullable), but the PLAN.md phase spec and the existing implementation declare them as non-nullable `number`. It is unclear whether these fields must accept null in this phase.
options: Keep non-nullable number as specified in PLAN.md and the existing model (treat the architecture's nullable variant as a design-time allowance not enforced now).
Align the model to number | null to match the reconciled architecture, requiring update of the interface, DTO, and tests.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy is logically deleted, never physically removed: softDelete sets deleted_at and all read operations (findById, findByLeaveTypeId, findAll) exclude rows where deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

A LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType via leaveTypeId; the model imports the LeaveType type from the Phase 3 leave-type model to express this relationship, and findByLeaveTypeId returns all non-deleted policies for that leave type.
On create, requiresManagerApproval and isActive default to true when omitted from the DTO; on update, only fields explicitly present in the partial DTO are modified and updated_at is refreshed.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array when none match); never throws on no-match. Delegates to the shared pg pool.
Returns LeavePolicy | null (null when not found or soft-deleted); never throws on no-match.
Returns LeavePolicy[] of all non-deleted policies ordered by policy name (empty array when none); never throws on empty table.
Persists a new row and returns the created LeavePolicy; relies on the database to reject constraint violations (e.g., duplicate/invalid leave_type_id) which propagate as pg errors.
Accepts a partial DTO; with no fields provided returns the existing non-deleted row without an UPDATE; returns null when the id is absent or already deleted; otherwise returns the updated row.
Returns boolean — true when a row was affected, false when the id does not exist or is already soft-deleted; never physically deletes.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeavePolicyRepository must follow the same structural pattern as the sibling LeaveTypeRepository: shared pg pool import, deleted_at IS NULL filtering on all reads, RETURNING * on create/update, dynamic field builder for update, softDelete via deleted_at = NOW() returning a boolean from rowCount, and ORDER BY the name column on findAll.

The LeavePolicy model must import the LeaveType interface from the Phase 3 leave-type model (not redefine it), establishing the leaveTypeId → LeaveType relationship consistently with how LeaveType itself imports LeaveTypeCode from shared types.
All repository SQL must execute through the shared pg pool exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts; no separate Pool instantiation or direct pg client usage is permitted in the leave module.

The leave-policy repository test must mirror the leave-type repository test's mocking strategy: jest.mock the shared db connection module to provide { pool: { query: jest.fn() } }, reset the mock in beforeEach, and assert both return values and the exact SQL/parameters passed to pool.query.

The leave barrel must re-export the LeavePolicy model and repository symbols alongside (not replacing) the existing Phase 3 LeaveType exports, preserving the single public entry point convention for the leave module.

integrationPoints.why: Provides the LeaveType interface imported by the LeavePolicy model to type the leaveTypeId relationship.
Provides the shared pg Pool used by LeavePolicyRepository for all leave_policies queries; the repository must not create its own pool.
The leave module barrel that downstream phases (LeaveBalance in Phase 5, LeaveService in Phase 8) import LeavePolicy and its repository from; this phase extends it with the new exports.
